🇲🇽🧒 <u>Mexico to spend 1.1 trillion pesos on children and teens in 2027</u>

Just over 1.102 trillion pesos goes to children and adolescents next year, according to Sipinna's Aurora Aguilar. The gap is real: of 12.2 million kids aged 0 to 5, 41.9% live in poverty and 56.9% lack social security. The 2026–2030 early-childhood strategy aims to cut chronic malnutrition from 14% to 7.5%, extreme poverty from 8.8% to 7.3%, and lift preschool attendance from 63.6% to 73% by 2030.

🇲🇽🔎 <u>Segob to searching mothers at the FGR sit-in: your protest is legitimate, let's talk</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez said the sit-in relatives of the disappeared have held for days at the Attorney General's Office is legitimate and must be attended, and that "there can be no impunity." The heads of the National Search Commission and the Victims Commission have met the group in person. She said people are located every day, that search takes more of her ministry's time than anything else, and opened the 24/7 National Immediate Search Alert command center to the press. "We're not letting up."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena runs its 2027 hopefuls through the Financial Intelligence Unit</u>

Morena president Ariadna Montiel told Contralínea the party is working with the UIF to block candidates whose wealth doesn't match their income. Files with criminal records plus UIF and SAT data were already delivered on the state coordinators picked for 2027, and the review covers anyone with a significant party post, not just candidates. "We have a commitment to the people that they be suitable, honest representatives." The opposition voted against the reform that created a vetting commission inside the INE.

🇲🇽💼 <u>SAT widens the simplified tax regime for small businesses in 2027</u>

Resico, the low-rate regime created in 2022, gets bigger in January. The income ceiling for individuals rises from 3.5 to 5 million pesos a year; for small companies, from 35 to 50 million. Income tax stays at 1% to 2.5%. The SAT says the regime has grown 130% since launch, with about 40,000 individuals and 1,400 companies signing up every week. Those who were pushed out can return if they're under the limit and up to date.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum closes APEC: ten deals with China, no trade treaty, T-MEC on track</u>

"We brought the representation of the people." Sheinbaum wrapped up her China trip calling it very productive: about ten memorandums of understanding and preliminary cooperation agreements signed with Beijing on economy, environment, energy, health, science and technology. She ruled out any trade treaty with China and said the relationship won't affect ties with the US, where the T-MEC review could close in December.

🇲🇽🎨 <u>Mexico's Culture Economy Outgrew the Whole Economy</u>

According to INEGI's Culture Satellite Account, Mexico's cultural economy generated 913.1 billion pesos in 2025, or 2.72% of GDP. It grew 1.7% in real terms, against 0.6% for the economy as a whole, El Economista reports. That is close to mining and metallurgy's 2.9%. Handicrafts are the biggest piece at 18.9% of cultural GDP, ahead of digital content at 17.8%. The weak spot was audiovisual (TV, film, radio, video games), which shrank 6.7%, its second straight year of decline.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum–Albanese: First Meeting, Gulf Oil on the Table</u>

Sheinbaum and Australian PM Anthony Albanese held their first bilateral on the APEC sidelines in Shenzhen. The centerpiece was Woodside's deep-water Trion project in the Gulf of Mexico, which Sheinbaum said is driving growth in Mexico's northeast. They also covered the port of Matamoros and trade, and Albanese said Australia ranks fourth among Mexico's largest foreign investors. Sheinbaum called the relationship "very active" and invited him to Mexico, which hosts APEC in 2028.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Segob: Behind Some Caravans, a Bus Business</u>

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez says some migrant caravans are fronts for a people-transport racket: "Some of the caravans have a type of organization where it has been detected that the leaders... are owners of bus lines." She called it a crime, though not necessarily one tied to organized crime, and said Mexico has arrested traffickers and will keep doing so. On Washington, Mexico cooperates "as a partner, as a neighbor of the United States and the Central American countries, but not as subordination."

🇲🇽🚆 <u>4,394 Km of Indigenous Roads, Built by the Communities Themselves</u>

Since December 2018, Mexico has built 578 caminos artesanales in Indigenous communities across 17 states. They add up to 4,394 km, built by local hands with local materials, for 21.474 billion pesos, INPI head Adelfo Regino reported. That is roughly the distance from Tapachula to Los Angeles. The program started in Analco, in Oaxaca's Sierra Norte, and has since reached the Montaña of Guerrero, the Meseta Purépecha, the Tarahumara and the Yaqui Valley. Another 343 roads are underway for 2026, with 400 work crews across 31 Indigenous peoples.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Oxfam: State Revenues Are a "Black Box"</u>

Mexico's states expected 3.2 trillion pesos in 2026, but only about 10% (328 billion) is money they raise themselves. The rest is federal transfers. Oxfam México's "Radiografía de los impuestos estatales 2026" calls local revenues a "caja negra," with little accountability and almost no public say over fiscal decisions. Local taxes cover 31.1% of Mexico City's income and just 2.2% of Chiapas's. States are budgeting 6.3% more tax for 2026, which is still 2.3% less in real terms than they actually collected in 2025.
